titulo.texto: Plumbate Vessel with an Effigy of Quetzalcóatl

frase_gancho.texto: A bearded face peers out from between the jaws of a coyote, made of shell.

puente_narrativo.texto: We continue with a small, shining piece: a face peering out from between the jaws of a coyote.

guion_corto.texto: This ceramic shines almost like metal. It is plumbate, a leaden clay with a vitrified finish. The vessel is a Toltec effigy 13 centimeters tall, 9.6 wide and 7 in diameter. It shows the head of a bearded man, whose face peers out from between the open jaws of a coyote helmet. It comes from the offering in the circular structure of El Corral, in Tula, and dates to the Early Postclassic. Sheets of shell were applied over the clay. Abalone forms the hair, the mustache and the beard, and mother-of-pearl shell forms the face and the feathers of the helmet. The teeth are made of bone and the pupils of obsidian. It is linked to Ehécatl-Quetzalcóatl and to Huehuecóyotl, the Old Coyote.

guion_largo.texto:
This ceramic shines almost like metal. It is called plumbate, or leaden, and has a metallic or vitrified finish. It was a luxury product, made in the coastal region of Chiapas and Guatemala. The Toltec traded it to the Central Highlands.

This vessel was found in Tula, in the offering in the circular structure of El Corral, and dates to the Early Postclassic. It measures 13 centimeters tall, 9.6 wide and 7 in diameter.

It represents the head of a bearded man. His face peers out from between the open jaws of a coyote helmet.

Look at how it is made. Sheets of shell were applied over the leaden clay. Abalone forms the hair, the mustache and the beard. Mother-of-pearl shell forms the feathers of the helmet and the face. The teeth and the fangs are carved in bone, and the pupils are of polished obsidian.

Who is he? He is linked to Ehécatl-Quetzalcóatl, the wind god who blew over the fields to bring the rain. He is also linked to Huehuecóyotl, the Old Coyote, god of dance and music. This is an iconographic identification. The museum also catalogs it under a more neutral name: Personage with an Animal Helmet.

One more detail. Over the coyote’s snout it wears a bone beak, a coyolómictl, which was used as an awl in autosacrifice rituals.

texto: Look for the bearded face peering out from between the coyote’s jaws.
Notice the hair and beard made of abalone shell.
Look at the obsidian pupils and the bone teeth.

texto.Material: Plumbate ceramic with a mosaic of mother-of-pearl shell, abalone, obsidian and bone
texto.Origin: Offering in the circular structure El Corral, Tula, Hidalgo
texto.Dimensions: 13 cm tall x 9.6 cm wide x 7 cm in diameter

texto.pregunta: Myth: This vessel was made in Tula, with local clay.
texto.respuesta: Reality: Plumbate ceramic is a luxury item and was produced on the coast of Chiapas and Guatemala. The Toltec traded it to the Central Highlands.
